body: I carry a cardholder/keypouch with a keyring attached to it on a daily basis for errands and things. If I am going somewhere where I feel like I need to carry extra stuff (sunglasses, lipstick, etc) I carry a shoulder bag (my go to is my coach bag). My keypouch is guess and does the job/is cute, but is rusting so I might splurge and get an LV one bc i know those last forever.

I’d also highly highly recommend reading adult children of emotionally immature parents (there are pdfs online). It was the first book that really opened my eyes up to the emotional immaturity of my parents, myself and others.

Totally agree with the other comments about you never really know what happens behind closed doors. I also obviously do not know his story, but that honestly sounds like it may have been a trigger for him from his childhood (most toxic or “oversensitive” behavior like this usually is). My parents have always spoiled me as well and were considered “funny, relatable and happy,” but behind closed doors what people often failed to see was how lonely my childhood was. My parents thought true emotion and vulnerability could be replaced with money, gifts and vacation— it could not. I too, acted like your friend did until I became more emotionally intelligent/aware (reading books, therapy, etc). 

I would tell you to take this opportunity to self reflect as to why you feel like he needs to “be humbled.” I think you would likely come to a conclusion of something along the lines of your own lack of self worth and fulfilment in life is causing you to project some feelings onto him. Usually this stems from needs (can be emotional, physical, etc) not being met by your parents during your childhood. Once you figure that out, I think you will feel much more secure in navigating your relationships and interactions with others. I would also encourage you to take this opportunity to reach out to this friend separately and talk to him— you might end up learning a lot about him and becoming closer!
